chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Ahmad ibn Abu Dawood, from Abdullah ibn Abdul Rahman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'Shall I teach you a supplication you can supplicate with, which we, the People of the Household, use whenever a matter worries us and we fear from the ruling authorities a matter we cannot face with, we supplicate with it?' I said, 'Yes, may my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah!'

He said: 'Say, O the One who existed before everything, and O the One Who Brought everything into being, and O the One Who would be Remaining after everything! Send Salawāt upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Do for me such and such.'

key_terms.لَا قِبَلَ لَنَا بِهِ: We cannot face it / We have no power over it

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for distress and fear of authorities in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Ahl al-Bayt's strategic use of divine attributes—specifically Allah's pre-existence (Qabl al-Shay'), creative power (Mukawwin), and permanence (Baqa')—to seek relief from political oppression and personal distress. This supplication reflects the Shia tradition of combining theological affirmation with practical petition, emphasizing reliance on God's eternal nature during times of uncertainty.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Ahmad Bin Abu Dawood, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘Heasws said to me: ‘Shall Iasws teach you a supplication you can supplicate with, which weasws, the Peopleasws of the Household tend to supplicate with whenever a matter worries usasws and weasws fear from the ruling authorities of a matter weasws cannot face with, weasws supplicate with it?’ I said, ‘Yes, may my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for youasws, O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww!’ Heasws said: ‘Say, ‘O the One who existed before everything, and O the One Who Brought everything into being, and O the One Who would be Remaining after everything! Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and Do for me such and such’’.
en.sarwar: 13. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Ahmad ibn abu Dawud from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Imam said to me, ‘Should I instinct you with a supplication so you can pray? We are a family that whenever something causes us pain or fear a ruler for something we cannot cope with, we pray to Allah with this supplication.’ I said, ‘Yes, may Allah keep my soul and the souls of my parents in service for your cause, O descendent of the Messenger of Allah.’

The Imam told me to say, ‘O the One who existed before everything, O the Giver of being to everything, O the Eternal Being after everything, grant al-Salat (favors) upon Muhammad and his family, and confer upon me such and such of my wishes and needs.’”
